## Try it in your browser, and stop getting alerted about AirPods

Two things worth leading with.

**There's now a browser emulator.** The actual firmware — the same C++ that ships to the ESP32 — compiled to WebAssembly and running client-side. Every screen, gesture, debounce and long-press is the real code, and colours are quantised to the panel's real 8-bit RGB332 so it looks like the hardware rather than better than it. Click the screen to touch it; there's a Trigger button for detections, since a browser has no radios. It's linked from the flasher page, or go straight to **/emulator/**.

**AirTag detection was firing on half of Apple's product line.** Two bugs stacked. The subtype filter accepted `0x07` — "Proximity Pairing", which AirPods and most Apple accessories broadcast constantly — and the caller gated the whole check behind a payload-length test, so any Apple advert too short to carry a subtype byte skipped filtering entirely and kept the AIRTAG type it got from the company ID alone. It failed open. Now it accepts only the Find My offline-finding beacons (`0x12`/`0x1E`), which a tag sends once it's been **separated from its owner** — the state that actually matters — and it fails closed on short payloads. A tag sitting next to its owner no longer reports, which is correct.

**Evil twin detection** is new: one network name beaconing from a second box that's a different vendor *and* disagrees about encryption. The obvious test — same SSID, different BSSID — is also every mesh network, and it fired constantly on a real one during development. What a mesh never does is argue with itself about security, so the Privacy bit is the discriminator.

The backgrounds got a serious pass too. A new **SYNTHWAVE** scene with a reflective floor (the boot splash uses it now as well), **WIREFRAME TUNNEL** rebuilt as a Tempest-style vector tube with a claw and climbing enemies, and **AQUARIUM** rebuilt around caustics on the seabed, a shoal running real flocking behaviour that scatters from the shark and re-forms, and a shark that actually swims instead of sliding sideways.

### The actually-useful part
- **Fixed**: AIRTAG matched nearly every Apple device — now Find My beacons only, and short payloads fail closed instead of open
- **Added**: browser emulator at `/emulator/` — the real firmware compiled to WebAssembly, no install
- **Added**: EVIL TWIN detection — a second AP claiming your network's name from different hardware while disagreeing about encryption
- **Added**: HUNT button on the alert screen, so you can start tracking a device without dismissing the alert and hunting for it in the log
- **Added**: SYNTHWAVE background, with a reflected sun that shimmers on the water; the boot splash now uses the same scene
- **Changed**: WIREFRAME TUNNEL is a Tempest-style vector tube — connected lanes, a claw on the rim, enemies climbing out of the vanishing point
- **Changed**: AQUARIUM rebuilt — caustic light on the seabed, a flocking shoal, depth haze, and a counter-shaded shark that flexes as it swims
- **Changed**: the main screen's counter row folds Samsung tags into TRACKER with the other trackers, freeing a column for EVIL
- **Fixed**: a 1px strip of leftover graphics under the title bar, on every screen — those rows belonged to nothing and kept whatever was last drawn there
- **Fixed**: Settings labels overlapped their values in portrait; rows now use a smaller size there
- **Fixed**: Blue Blur had a third quill standing straight up that didn't belong
- **Fixed**: new detection types could arrive switched off for anyone who'd opened TYPE FILTER before upgrading
- **Changed**: boot splash title and subtitle are outlined, so they read against the sunset behind them
